page: Microsoft Azure E16-8as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Easv7 server family. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, this server features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. The server does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scores all placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth is also average, measuring 50.41 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 33.95 GB/sec for large block write operations. Large-model LLM prompt processing is relatively weak, though text generation with smaller models performs in the top 25%.

Given its high memory density of 16 GB per vCPU and strong single-core performance, the E16-8as_v7 offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads without the cost overhead of additional vCPUs. It is well-suited for memory-intensive applications such as relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, text processing pipelines, and lightweight language model inference.
